author: श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थभगवत्पादाचार्य
commentary:
कियत्पर्यन्तम् अवश्यं कर्तव्यानि मुमुक्षुणैवं कर्माणीति ? आह- यदेति ॥ निर्वेदं नितरां लाभम् । प्रयोगात् - ‘तस्माद् ब्राह्मणः पाण्डित्यं निर्विद्य बाल्येन तिष्ठासेत् ।’ इत्यादि । 

न हि तत्र वैराग्यमुपपद्यते । तथा सति ‘पाण्डित्याद्’ इति स्यात् । न च ज्ञानिनां भगवन्महिमादिश्रवणे विरक्तिर्भवति । 

‘आत्मारामा हि मुनयो निर्ग्राह्या अप्युरुक्रमे । 

कुर्वन्त्यहैतुकीं भक्तिम् इत्थम्भूतगुणो हरिः ॥’ इति वचनात् । 

अनुष्ठानाच्च शुकादीनाम् । न च तेषां (फलं) सुखं नास्ति । तस्यैव महत्सुखत्वात् तेषाम्- 

‘या निर्वृतिस्तनुभृतां तव पादपद्मध्यानाद् भवज्जनकथाश्रवणेन वा स्यात् । सा ब्रह्मणि स्वमहिमन्यपि नाथ मा भूत् किम्वन्तकासिलुलितात् पततां विमानात् ॥’ इत्यादिवचनात् । 

तेषामप्युपासनादिफलस्य साधितत्वात् । 

तारतम्याधिगतेश्च । तथा हि- यदि तारतम्यं न स्यात्, ‘नाऽत्यन्तिकं विगणयन्त्यपि ते प्रसादम्’, ‘नैकात्मतां मे स्पृहयन्ति केचित्’ ‘एकत्व(मित्युत)मप्युत दीयमानं न गृह्णन्ति’ इति मुक्तिमप्यनिच्छतामपि मोक्ष एव फलम्, तमिच्छतामपि स (एव) भवति सुप्रतीकादीनामिति कथम् अनिच्छतां स्तुतिरुपपन्ना स्यात् ? वचनाच्च -

‘यथा भक्तिविशेषोऽत्र दृश्यते पुरुषोत्तमे । तथा मुक्तिविशेषोऽपि ज्ञानिनां लिङ्गभेदने ॥ 

योगिनां भिन्नलिङ्गानाम् आविर्भूतस्वरूपिणाम् । प्राप्तानां परमानन्दं तारतम्यं सदैव हि ॥’ इति (इत्याद्युक्तेः )। 

‘न त्वाम् अतिशयिष्यन्ति मुक्तावपि कथञ्चन । 

मद्भक्तियोगाज्ज्ञानाच्च सर्वान् अतिशयिष्यसि ॥’ इति च । 

साम्यवचनं तु प्राचुर्यविषयम्, दुःखाभावविषयं च । तच्चोक्तम्-‘दुःखाभावः परानन्दो लिङ्गभेदः समा(मो) मताः(तः) । 

तथाऽपि परमानन्दो ज्ञानभेदात्तु भिद्यते ॥’ इति नारायणाष्टाक्षरकल्पे । 

अतो न वैराग्यं श्रुतादौ अत्र विवक्षितम् । न च सङ्कोचे मानं किञ्चिद् विद्यमान इतरत्र प्रयोगे । महद्भिः श्रवणीयस्य श्रुतस्य च वेदादेः फलं प्राप्स्यसीत्यर्थः ॥५२ ॥
translation:
Acharya Madhva uses this text to answer a fundamental question: How long must a person seeking liberation (mumukṣu) perform actions, and what does the word Nirveda actually mean here? In doing so, he presents an extensive, uncompromising defense of the concept of Ananda-Taratamya (the eternal hierarchy of bliss among liberated souls in Moksha), which is a signature pillar of Dvaita Vedanta. 

To answer the question: 'Up to what point must actions definitely be performed by a seeker of liberation (mumukṣu)?' Krishna speaks the verse beginning with “Yadā” (When). Acharya Madhva defines the word Nirveda here not as worldly detachment or indifference (vairāgya), but as 'complete, supreme gain/attainment' (nitarāṁ lābham) of spiritual reality. This meaning is established due to its scriptural usage in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad: “Therefore, a knower of Brahman, having completely gained (nirvidya) spiritual scholarship, should desire to remain like a child.” For in that Upanishadic context, the meaning of 'detachment' or 'disgust' is not logical or applicable. If it meant detachment, the text would have used the ablative form “pāṇḍityād” (detached from scholarship). Furthermore, it is impossible for enlightened souls (jñānīs) to ever develop detachment, indifference, or disgust (viraktiḥ) toward hearing the glorious pastimes and majesties of the Supreme Lord. Because of the famous scriptural decree in the Srimad Bhagavatam (1.7.10): “Even those sages who are completely satisfied within the self (ātmārāmāḥ) and are entirely free from material bondage, still perform unalloyed, causeless devotional service (ahaitukīṁ bhaktim) unto the wide-striding Lord Urukrama (Vishnu). Such are the wonderful, transcendental qualities of Lord Hari.” And this is seen through the actual practical behavior of perfect liberated souls like Shuka Deva and others. Nor can it be said that they lack the fruit of happiness; for hearing about God is itself the highest, ultimate bliss for them. As declared by the demigods in scripture: “O Lord, that profound ecstasy (nirvṛtiḥ) which embodied souls experience by meditating upon Your lotus feet, or by hearing the narrations of Your pastimes spoken by Your devotees—that bliss is not to be found even in the non-dual realization of Brahman, nor in one's own spiritual majesty. What then to speak of those whose heavenly airplanes are shattered by the sword of time, causing them to fall?” For even for those liberated souls, the ultimate fruit of their spiritual worship (upāsanā) has already been perfectly accomplished.

And this must be accepted because of the systematic understanding of the graded hierarchy (Tāratamya) of souls. To explain: If this eternal hierarchy of bliss did not exist in liberation, then consider scriptural statements like: “They do not value even the ultimate liberation if it is devoid of service,” “Certain devotees never desire oneness with Me,” and “Even when absolute oneness is offered to them, they do not accept it.” If liberation were identical for everyone, then for those pure devotees who do not even desire it, liberation is the fruit; and for those who explicitly desire it (like Sage Supratika and others), that very same static liberation is the fruit. If that were the case, how could the scriptural praise (stutiḥ) of those devotees who refuse to accept standard liberation be logical or justified? (It would be meaningless unless their liberation is of a uniquely higher, blissful quality). And this is explicitly confirmed by scriptural statements: “Just as a specific distinction and gradation in devotion (bhakti-viśeṣaḥ) is observed toward the Supreme Person (Purushottama) in this world, exactly so, a specific distinction and gradation in liberation (mukti-viśeṣaḥ) exists for the wise souls upon the shattering of their subtle bodies (linga-bhedane). For those yogis whose subtle bodies have been dissolved, whose innate spiritual forms have fully manifested, and who have achieved the supreme bliss—a structural hierarchy (tāratamya) exists among them for all eternity.” And as the Lord declares to a supreme soul (like Chaturmukha Brahma): “Even in the state of final liberation, no one shall ever surpass or equal you in any manner. Because of your supreme devotion, yoga, and realization, you shall eternally surpass all other liberated souls.”

On the other hand, scriptural statements that speak of 'equality' (sāmya) among the liberated souls actually refer to the general abundance of bliss common to all, and to the absolute absence of suffering (duḥkha-abhāva) shared equally by everyone. And this is explicitly clarified in the Nārāyaṇa-Aṣṭākṣara-Kalpa: “The total absence of misery, the experience of supreme spiritual ecstasy, and the dissolution of the subtle material body are considered identical and equal for all liberated souls. Nevertheless, the specific quantity and depth of that supreme ecstasy varies and differs precisely based on the intrinsic differences in their original spiritual knowledge and capacity.”

Therefore, 'detachment' or 'disgust' toward hearing the scriptures is absolutely not what is intended by the word Nirveda in this verse. Nor is there any valid proof to narrow down or limit the vast scope of this word, given its glorious usage elsewhere in the Vedas. The ultimate meaning of Krishna's words to Arjuna is: “You shall confidently attain the supreme, true spiritual fruit of all the sacred Vedic scriptures which have been heard by you, and which are eternally fit to be heard by the greatest of sages.”
